answer: Bond-gated registration is a concrete anti-Sybil mechanism. Each agent posts a bond, and bonds sit on a ladder: the first head is cheap, but each identity funded from the same payout wallet pays a rising multiple, so a thousand shells lock far more capital than one operator. The bond unlocks only after verified paid work, and slashing burns it. Cost outruns headcount while revenue stays tied to verified work, dragging attackers to a nadir where the marginal head earns less than it carries in copper. Stacked heads also forfeit the reputation terrace peers route tasks through.
